outcome: The general conjecture (la(G) ≤ ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉) remains open, but two results in the window advance it: a July 2025 preprint improves the best known general upper bound on la(G) from Δ/2 + O(√Δ·log⁴Δ) (Lang–Postle 2023) to Δ/2 + O(log n), an exponential improvement in the error term whenever Δ = Ω(n^ε); and a December 2025 preprint proves the exact conjectural bound for 2k-regular graphs whose girth is at least 2k (with weaker bounds for smaller girth thresholds), settling a restricted case rather than the general conjecture.
summary: The conjecture, posed by Akiyama, Exoo and Harary (1980), states la(G) ≤ ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ for every simple graph G, and remains open in general as of 22 September 2026. Two genuine but partial advances occurred in the window. (1) Christoph, Draganić, Girão, Hurley, Michel and Müyesser, 'New bounds for linear arboricity and related problems' (arXiv:2507.20500, submitted 28 Jul 2025, v1 only), verified directly by fetching both the abstract page and the PDF, prove la(G) ≤ Δ/2 + O(log n), an exponential improvement over the previous best general bound Δ/2 + O(√Δ·log⁴Δ) due to Lang and Postle (2023, Combinatorica), whenever Δ = Ω(n^ε). This is squarely a bound moving on the stated problem's own quantity (la(G)), not a variant, so it is scope-relevant progress; however, it does not close the gap to the conjectured ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉, so the general conjecture is still open. No mention of AI/LLM assistance appears anywhere in the paper (checked PDF text and acknowledgements/funding footnotes, which cite only SNSF and ERC grants); ai_role is therefore none. (2) Tapas Kumar Mishra, 'The Linear Arboricity Conjecture for Graphs with Large Girth' (arXiv:2512.11240, submitted 12 Dec 2025, v1 only), verified directly the same way, proves the exact conjectural bound la(G) ≤ k+1 for 2k-regular graphs with girth g(G) ≥ 2k, via 2-factor decomposition and an auxiliary flow network, with weaker bounds given as girth thresholds relax further. This is a genuine case of the stated problem — a restriction to a class of graphs (large girth, fixed regularity) rather than a change to the question — so it counts as partial progress under §3.1, in the same spirit as prior girth/degeneracy-restricted results in this literature (e.g. arXiv:2007.06066 on low-degeneracy graphs). No AI mention found in the PDF text. Both preprints are single-version, unrefereed as of this writing (no citing papers, no MathOverflow or blog discussion found), though the July 2025 paper's author group is well-established (Oxford-affiliated combinatorialists with ERC/SNSF funding) and the December 2025 paper's sole author is an independently verifiable academic (Assistant Professor, NIT Rourkela). Status is coded 'partial' rather than 'progress' because the December 2025 result settles an actual case of the conjecture outright (not merely a bound), which under §6.1 takes priority in describing what happened; the July 2025 bound improvement is noted as additional progress in this same summary rather than given its own record, per the instructions to fold multiple events into one summary. A third, lower-confidence item surfaced by the research pass — a JCMCC (Journal of Combinatorial Mathematics and Combinatorial Computing) Vol. 130 paper by 'Yuina Tanaka' claiming the conjecture for certain graph products, accepted 30 Jan 2026 — is not included as the basis for this record's status because it has no arXiv preprint, the author could not be independently verified via Google Scholar/ResearchGate/arXiv author search, and JCMCC's indexing status has reportedly been questioned; it is noted here for completeness but not relied upon. Wikipedia's own 'Linear arboricity' article (last edited 26 Dec 2025, checked directly) is stale and still cites only the 2018/2020 Ferber–Fox–Jain bound, omitting both Lang–Postle (2023) and the two 2025 preprints described above — confirming that no one has yet updated the encyclopedia to reflect this window's progress.
competing_reading: One could argue the July 2025 bound-improvement result, being a genuine advance but not itself a settled case, should be classified as 'progress' with the December 2025 girth result mentioned only secondarily, or that the two should be split into a decision about which is 'the' decisive event. I chose 'partial' because a full case of the conjecture (large-girth 2k-regular graphs) was proved exactly, which is a stronger and more specific kind of movement than an error-term improvement, and the instructions direct choosing one decisive event while describing others in the summary. Someone weighting the bound-improvement as more consequential (since it applies to essentially all high-degree graphs, whereas the girth result is a narrower structural restriction) might reasonably default to 'progress' instead.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement proving la(G) ≤ ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ unconditionally for all graphs, or a counterexample refuting it, would settle the general conjecture. Independent citation, refereeing, or a follow-up paper corroborating either 2025 preprint's correctness would raise confidence in the current partial results.
